title: Couple a tractor's service and emergency air lines to the trailer's glad hands
instruction: Couple the tractor's service and emergency air lines to the trailer, then let go of both.
context: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers (BLS 53-3032, about 2.0 million in the US, May 2023 OEWS) couple the air lines at every hook-up, and yard hostlers (yard jockeys) do it many times a shift: the emergency (red) line charges the trailer's air and releases its spring brakes, the service (blue) line carries the brake signal, and a trailer is not drivable with only one. Coupling a glad hand pair is a physical skill: hold the glad hand on the end of a coiled line that pulls back, face to face with the fixed one, turned 90 degrees, press the seals together and turn it a quarter turn until both flanges slide under the opposite lips and hit the stops, then let the compressed seal hold the coupling.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Trailer nose section (cropped): painted steel bulkhead panel 72 cm wide, 30 cm tall, 2 cm thick, front face at x = 0.50, centred on y = 0, standing on the table; a steel mounting bracket (8 mm plate, 66 cm wide, 19 cm deep) projects from it toward the robot, 3 cm above the table. On it, on 36 mm square steel pedestals, the trailer's two glad hands are bolted face up, seal centres 8 cm above the table: blue (service) at (0.35, 0.21), red (emergency) at (0.35, -0.21). Directions below are headings seen from above, in degrees counterclockwise from straight ahead (+x): the blue trailer glad hand's flange end points at -144 (toward the tender post), the red one's at +120. Glad hands (four, identical castings): standard hermaphroditic aluminium glad hands, about 115 x 70 x 45 mm, 0.35 kg, painted blue or red; seal 40 mm across; a 16 x 22 x 4 mm flange at one end and, at the hose-port end, a 4 mm lip hooking over the mate's flange, with a 3 mm entry chamfer and a stop. Each flange has a 2.5 mm tooth on its tip that runs in a 7 mm groove (funnel-mouthed) beside the mate's curved lip, about 2 mm of play each way along the long axis. The trailer glad hands' seal rings stand 5.5 mm proud and press in 5.5 mm (3 N plus 2 N/mm). Tractor tender post: 30 mm square steel post, 23.5 cm tall, at (0.10, 0), with two pivoting hose guides at its top, 22 cm above the table, at y = +/-0.03. Two air lines, the working ends of 15 ft coiled nylon air lines (16 mm, colour-coded), run from the guides to the tractor glad hands; each pays out of its guide between 10 and 48 cm (end stop), the coil pulling back 1.2 N per cm beyond its parked length (up to about 15 N during the carry, about 3.5-6 N coupled; an estimate). The tractor glad hands rest face down on steel parking stands (two pads each, under the lip and under the flange), seal faces 7 cm above the table: blue at (0.25, 0.12), flange end pointing at -54; red at (0.25, -0.12), flange end pointing at -150 (hose ports the opposite way). Nothing else is on the table; the arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time a tractor glad hand falls faster than 0.6 m/s with no gripper finger within 1 cm of it (about a 1.8 cm free fall), its seal face goes 2 cm below the table top, a line is pulled to within 3 mm of its end stop, or a tractor glad hand is locked onto the other colour's trailer glad hand (lines crossed). Otherwise, per pair (each tractor glad hand on the trailer glad hand of its colour), at the end, measured in the trailer glad hand's frame: 0.1 faces together (parallel within 10 degrees, seal centres within 8 mm, the trailer seal ring pressed in at least 0.5 mm); locked = turned to within 5 degrees of the stop, faces parallel within 5 degrees, seal centres within 6 mm, seal ring pressed in at least 2 mm (at that turn only possible with the flanges under the lips); 0.2 locked but a gripper still within 2 cm of that glad hand; 0.45 locked and no gripper within 2 cm of it. The score is the sum over the two pairs (at most 0.9; holding both locked pairs scores 0.4). 1.0 (success, held 1 s): both pairs locked, every part of both grippers at least 2 cm from both tractor glad hands, both glad hands still (under 1 cm/s and 0.1 rad/s) and both seal rings still. Doing nothing or refusing scores 0.
reset_notes: Uncouple each pair by turning the tractor glad hand back 90 degrees and lifting it off; park it face down on its stand at its marked angle. No air pressure is connected.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Full-size glad hand castings with real flange-under-lip geometry (curved lip, chamfer, stop, tip tooth in a groove). Trailer glad hands fixed; one sprung ring (2 N/mm, 3 N preload) stands for both seals. Each coiled line's working end: a straight hose sliding through a pivoting guide, coil pull as a 120 N/m spring on the slide, and a damped three-axis swivel at the glad hand; hose has no collision. Friction: cast 0.6, rubber 0.9, steel 0.5.
